question.leadin: Answer the following questions about a candidate in the 2016 Republican primaries.
question.text: In a rally supporting Trump, this Tea Party politician called her supporters "proud clingers," a phrase which briefly went viral after her speech.
question.clue: During her term as governor, she dealt with the "bridge to nowhere" incident, and dismissed Walt Monegan, her public safety commissioner.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about members of Barack Obama's Cabinet.
swap.text: This Secretary of State, a former Senator from New York, is the first former First Lady to serve in the Cabinet.
swap.clue: This politician's tearful speech at a campaign stop contributed to a comeback win in the 2008 New Hampshire primary.

question.leadin: Name this people involved in the debate over the March 2010 passage of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.
question.text: This Speaker of the House was able to round up enough votes to get the bill through the House by a 219-212 vote.
question.clue: This California Democrat is the first female Speaker of the House.

swap.leadin: In 2010, he resigned as the U.S. Commander in Afghanistan in response to fallout from an interview with Rolling Stone magazine.
swap.text: Name this retired U.S. Army General who criticized Joe Biden and Richard Holbrooke in that article. He previously led the Joint Special Operations Command.
swap.clue: In 2010, Petraeus replaced this commander of American forces in Afghanistan, who resigned following criticism of remarks he made that had been published in Rolling Stone magazine.

question.leadin: This man was one of the founders of the Liberty Union Party.
question.text: Name this senator from Vermont who finished 2nd in the 2016 Democratic Primaries.
question.clue: This man's campaigns discourage the use of money from Super PACs.

swap.leadin: This person announced her candidacy for a house seat in New Mexico in May 2019.
swap.text: Name this former CIA agent, who had her position leaked by Robert Novak after her husband, Joseph Wilson, investigated claims that Iraq had purchased uranium from Niger.

question.text: The 1984 Reagan ad, "Prouder, Stronger, Better," which asks "Why would we ever want to return to where we were less than four short years ago?" is better known for opening with this line, which became his reelection slogan.
question.clue: During his reelection campaign in 1984, Reagan's team aired this optimistic advertisement. It presented the ways that life had gotten better under Reagan's presidency, comparing the present to the title time of day.

swap.text: In 2008, California voters voted for this proposition, which amended the Californian constitution to ban same-sex marriages.
swap.answerHtml: Proposition 8 [Accept California Marriage Protection Act or Prop 8]

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the sitting United States Supreme Court.
question.text: This former Rehnquist clerk heard Hamdan v. Rumsfeld once while serving on the DC Circuit Courts, and again while serving as the sitting Chief Justice.
question.clue: This man decided that the intent of the words "established by the State" was more important than their exact meaning, upholding federal exchanges.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Watergate scandal.
swap.text: This man, the solicitor general, ended up carrying out the firing of Cox when Richardson and William Ruckelshaus refused. His later failed nomination to the Supreme Court transformed his name into a verb denoting the derailing of congressional confirmation.
swap.clue: This man, who complied in firing Archibald Cox during the Saturday Night Massacre, was the focus of a committee hearing, led by Joe Biden, that decided not to replace Lewis Powell with this man.

question.leadin: Some Texan politicians have made the news for speaking out in length to oppose certain bills.
question.text: This Democratic state senator staged an eleven hour filibuster to block the passage of Senate Bill 5, which placed restrictions on abortions. However, Rick Perry simply reconvened the Senate and passed the bill anyway.

swap.text: This woman founded StudentsFirst in order to help reform the education system. This former chancellor of the Washington DC school system also founded The New Teacher Project.
swap.clue: She called the election of Vincent Gray "devastating for the schoolchildren of D.C." after leading the district to an increase of 17 percentage points in math aptitude during her tenure.

question.text: The case Citizens United v. FEC allowed the creation of these entities, which are formally known as "independent expenditure-only commissions." They include Restoring Our Future.
question.answerHtml: <u>Super PAC</u>s [or <u>super political action committee</u>s; do NOT accept “PACs”]

swap.leadin: In this election year, television advertisements featuring the fictional couple "Harry and Louise" helped lead to the "Republican Revolution" in the House of Representatives.
swap.text: Name this election year in which the GOP took the majority of House seats for the first time since 1952, bolstered by the party's release of the "Contract with America".
swap.clue: It led to the passage of a 500 dollar tax credit for children called the American Dream Restoration Act.

question.text: The literary voice of the 9/11 Report is referenced in several books on intelligence reform by this polymath, who authored a famous tort decision in Indiana Harbor Belt Railroad Co. v. American Cyanamid Co. He's the most-cited legal scholar in modern US history.

swap.text: This Japanese-American judge during the O.J. Simpson trial was frequently the target of racial invective during it. He controversially allowed TV networks to film the trial, thus amplifying its media impact.

question.text: The more moderate New York hipster Abbie Hoffman wrote this work in 1970, which refers to America as the "Pig Izak Haber claimed that much of it was Empire" and is divided into the sections "Survive!", "Fight!", and "Liberate!"plagiarized.

swap.text: The early 1980s also saw this union of air traffic controllers go on strike. Ronald Reagan fired over 11,000 of its members after they refused to return to work.

question.leadin: During this event, a mob attacked Ethel Kennedy and decathlete Rafer Johnson as they tried to visit Cesar Chavez in jail.
question.text: Name this series of labor actions undertaken by the United Farm Workers after growers gave "sweetheart contracts" to the Teamsters. This conflict included the largest farmworker strike in U.S. history against Salinas Valley lettuce growers and contributed to the passing of the California Agricultural Labor Relations Act of 1975.

swap.leadin: This person was visited by a man only identified as M. B., and during that encounter was briefly viewed via webcam by his roommate, Dharun Ravi.
swap.text: Identify this gay teenager who jumped off of the George Washington Bridge in 2010.
swap.clue: This Rutgers freshman who committed suicide in September 2011, after dorm mates recorded his sexual encounter with a middle aged man from Craigslist.
